These rules are for the agent's later session in /workspace. They do not apply to you: implement system enforcement for each rule with its enforcer, at its trigger, on its target.

Rule R7: 生成的代码文件必须满足：单个函数的规模不得大于 60 行

- Route: Semgrep (Analysis › Code scans › Semgrep) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Function / method (Source code › Function / method)
- The check, by the enforcer: A pattern-based static analyzer. A rule is a code pattern that Semgrep matches against each file's syntax tree, for many languages (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML script blocks, Bash, …). Check: `semgrep scan --config <rules.yml> --error --metrics=off --quiet <file>` (exit 1 on a finding; `--json` for a report) Rules: `rules: [{id: <id>, languages: [<language>], severity: ERROR, message: "<what to change>", pattern: "<code pattern>"}]`; Semgrep matches syntax, it cannot compute values (a length, a count): let Semgrep find the code (`--json` gives each match's file, start and end lines), and compute the value from that in a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py)
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tools (it sees the new content); file permissions (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/file-permissions.md) (the write fails)
- What it reads, by the target: A function or a method. Where: in the source files; read them with a parser (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_python.py, /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_js.py), or with Semgrep patterns Which files: every file that holds code, decided when the check runs (/opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md); take embedded code out of its container first (a `<script>` in HTML), then parse it
- Tools: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/semgrep: installed already; call each by this full path, since the agent's PATH does not have that folder
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/analysis/code-scans/semgrep.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/function-method.md

Rule R5: 无论生成哪个代码文件，其起始第一行都必须严格添加 -*- coding: utf-8 -*- 以声明编码

- Route: pre-commit (Gates › Git hooks › pre-commit) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Source file (Source code › Source file)
- The check, by the enforcer: A framework that runs the checks in a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file when a commit is made. Check: a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (local hooks: `repo: local`, `entry: <check>`) and `pre-commit install`; or `pre-commit run --files <file>`
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tools (it sees the new content); file permissions (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/file-permissions.md) (the write fails)
- What it reads, by the target: A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages. Code also sits inside other files: a `<script>` or `<style>` in HTML, a notebook cell, a code block in Markdown. A file of an unknown kind is checked, not passed.
- Tools: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/pre-commit: installed already; call each by this full path, since the agent's PATH does not have that folder
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/gates/git-hooks/pre-commit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md

Rule R6: 你所生成的任何一个代码文件，其开头处都需另起一行进行清晰的注释声明：“AI-Assisted: Initial draft generated by Claude Code; reviewed and modified by author.”

- Route: pre-commit (Gates › Git hooks › pre-commit) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Source file (Source code › Source file)
- The check, by the enforcer: A framework that runs the checks in a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file when a commit is made. Check: a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (local hooks: `repo: local`, `entry: <check>`) and `pre-commit install`; or `pre-commit run --files <file>`
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tools (it sees the new content); file permissions (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/file-permissions.md) (the write fails)
- What it reads, by the target: A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages. Code also sits inside other files: a `<script>` or `<style>` in HTML, a notebook cell, a code block in Markdown. A file of an unknown kind is checked, not passed.
- Tools: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/pre-commit: installed already; call each by this full path, since the agent's PATH does not have that folder
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/gates/git-hooks/pre-commit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md

The work for these rules comes as nodes, one at a time; when you reply to a node, the harness checks it. The nodes: check-R7, check-R5, check-R6, binding-1.
Build exactly what each rule's route says. If a part of a route cannot work here, write why in /opt/enforce/deviations.json ({"R<n>": "<why>"}) and build the nearest thing that keeps the rest of the route.


Done before this node:
- check-R7 (R7): done, checked; /opt/enforce/checks/R7, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/flag, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/pass
- check-R5 (R5): done, checked; /opt/enforce/checks/R5, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R5/flag, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R5/pass
- check-R6 (R6): done, checked; /opt/enforce/checks/R6, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R6/flag, /opt/enforce/fixtures/R6/pass

Node binding-1 (4 of 4): make the agent's Claude Code run the checks of R7, R5, R6 (/opt/enforce/checks/R7, /opt/enforce/checks/R5, /opt/enforce/checks/R6) at PreToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit and at PostToolUse on Bash, in /workspace/.claude/settings.json: the project's settings, which load for the agent in /workspace and not for your own session; hooks that other rules' bindings already put there stay. The hook reads the file as it will be after the write, from the hook's tool_input (Write: content; Edit and MultiEdit: the file on disk with the edits applied); a shell command's writes cannot be seen before it runs, so after each shell command the files it changed; it runs every check on every file it reads (or on the reply) and reports all their violations in one message; on a violation it should refuse the write (permissionDecision "deny") with the check's message; after a shell command, exit 2 with it. Block only the violation, so the agent can fix its work and go on.
Done when: `/opt/enforce-harness/try --check` reports nothing, and each test case of R7, R5, R6, given to the hooks as the agent would make it (written by a file tool and by a shell command, or sent as the reply), is blocked with a message naming its rule when it breaks the rule, and passes when it follows it. The harness checks this when you reply.
